attempts.raw_response: The dogs, named Jessie, Kip, Hetty, Otto, and Timmy, are based at the University of Lincoln. They have been trained to work with students who may be feeling anxious or homesick, particularly during exam periods. Research suggests that interaction with dogs can lower blood pressure and reduce cortisol levels. The university plans to study the impact of the programme on student mental health, collecting data to see whether the presence of the dogs makes a measurable difference to attendance and academic performance. Students can book sessions with the dogs or encounter them in common areas around campus. The initiative follows similar programmes in other institutions, though Lincoln claims its approach is more structured and evidence-based than previous efforts elsewhere.
